runs.title: EA shuts BioWare: what's actually happening?

Find out exactly what was announced: how many jobs are going, what happens to BioWare, whether the next Mass Effect game has been cancelled, and any statement or comment from EA. runs.answer: On 21 October 2026 EA confirmed it is shutting down BioWare and cutting about 400 jobs. Per Bloomberg's reporting (cited by The Verge and Polygon), roughly 400 EA employees are being let go — about 3% of the company and around 50 of them at BioWare; The Verge and TNW both frame the 400 figure as Bloomberg-reported. BioWare is closing entirely, including its Edmonton workspace, with its official social accounts posting: "Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending." Yes — the next Mass Effect game (announced in 2020, colloquially "Mass Effect 5") is cancelled: in their staff memo EA president/chief studios officer Cam Weber and president/COO David Tinson wrote that "we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we're closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace." Their comment continued: "BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly," adding that EA had "taken a hard look at our business" and will focus on pr

runs.title: Harry and Meghan: why they moved back to UK
runs.prompt: Prince Harry has given a new interview explaining why he and Meghan Markle moved their family from California back to the UK. Find out what he actually said: the specific reasons he gave for the move. Use a source that is not paywalled. runs.answer: In GQ's "One More Question" interview with Zach Baron, published 20 October 2026 (titled "Prince Harry: 'This Grief Can Either Hold You Back or Help You Grow'"), Harry gave these reasons for the move: "Opportunities for the family. Being able to put the kids in a British school has meant a lot to me. I didn't know how important it was to me"—he said the children (seven and five) are "loving it" and gaining "two completely different cultural experiences." He also cited being "back closer to my family and to be back on UK soil for longer than a few days or a week here or there," and wanting "to show my kids where I grew up and have them have the experiences to some extent that I had, the good rather than necessarily the bad." He added it wasn't long-planned ("when certain stars align... we lean into that"), that his attitude to the media has changed, that "it's good to be outside of the US for the next few months, perhaps. Let things settle down," and he spoke of grieving strained family relationships he is trying to repair.
